hand: Shadow Dexterous Hand, Allegro Hand, TriFinger
success_criterion: orientation-matching tolerance of 0.4 rad (OpenAI's tolerance; also tested at 0.1 rad), reported via consecutive successes per episode
headline_metric: wall-clock time to reach 20 consecutive successes (Shadow Hand OpenAI reproduction); real-world success rate (TriFinger)
headline_value: >20 consecutive successes in <1 hour (1x A100) vs 30 hours (OpenAI's 6144-CPU-core + 8-V100 GPU cluster); TriFinger real-world mean success rate 55%
note_gaps: Table 14's Shadow Hand OpenAI policy observation breakdown ('5x Finger joints position: 3') is ambiguous in the flattened markdown table and may mean 15, not 3; verify against the original PDF before quoting the exact observation dimension.
contact_model: Rigid-body contacts via PhysX; contact geometry can be primitive shapes or meshes loaded from URDF/MJCF (Sec. 2.2); net contact forces exposed per-rigid-body via the Tensor API (Table 1, Get-only). No explicit statement of convex-vs-mesh contact generation or per-pair contact-point count. Shadow Hand tendons simulated via PhysX Fixed Tendon mechanics: spring+damping force proportional to deviation from rest length, propagated through a tendon-joint tree (Sec. 3, Appendix A.1).
solver: Temporal Gauss-Seidel (TGS) solver (Sec. 3, ref. 18), not classic PGS/LCP: folds sub-stepping into a per-body accumulated velocity-delta buffer projected onto the constraint Jacobians. Table 3 exposes two user-tunable iteration knobs, Position iterations (biased, velocity+positional-error-correcting) and Velocity iterations (unbiased, velocity-error-only-correcting); no default numeric values for these are given in the main text.
throughput: Shadow Hand: 150,000 parallel environment steps/sec at 16,384 environments, single NVIDIA A100 GPU (Sec. 5.3); Shadow Hand OpenAI reproduction (feed-forward): >20 consecutive successes in <1 hour on 1x A100 vs. 30 hours on OpenAI's cluster of 384x16-core CPUs (6144 cores total) + 8x NVIDIA V100 GPUs (Sec. 6.4.1).
hands_shipped: TriFinger (3-finger, 9-DoF manipulator; the paper itself says this is not a hand)
